## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The changes need revision: deleting the defaults file breaks its existing loader, port validation rejects a valid boundary value, and configuration failures are silently hidden.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file makes every call to `app.startup.load_defaults()` raise `FileNotFoundError`, because that function still reads it. Please restore the file or update the loader with replacement defaults. — Existing default-configuration loading stops working.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, although the documented range includes 65535. Please change the upper comparison to `<= 65535`. — Callers reject a valid TCP port.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — For a missing file or malformed JSON, `load_config(path)` catches the exception and returns `{}` without reporting the failure. Please propagate the exception or provide a caller-visible error. — Callers cannot distinguish configuration failure from a successfully loaded empty configuration.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The trailing-dot branch has no test: the existing normalization test only passes `"Example.COM"`. Please assert that `normalize_host("Example.COM.")` returns `"example.com"`. — A regression that retains the trailing dot would pass the current tests.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — For `normalize_host("")`, the docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the code executes `return ""`. Please align the documentation and behavior. — Callers following the documented return contract receive a different value.

## Strengths
- The milliseconds test asserts that `"1500ms"` becomes `1.5`, checking fractional-second conversion.
- The configuration success test reads an actual temporary JSON file and checks the parsed result.
